ROBI.about: Robi Axiata PLC is a mobile network operator serving Bangladesh, majority-owned by Malaysia's Axiata Group Berhad (61.82% stake) and Bharti International Singapore (28.18%), with the remaining share held by the general public via the Dhaka and Chittagong Stock Exchanges. Headquartered in Dhaka, the company describes itself as evolving from a traditional telecom operator ("telco") into a broader digital-services provider ("techco"), built around a nationwide 4G network reaching 98.98% population coverage across 19,043 sites.
ROBI.products: Core mobile connectivity — voice, SMS, and 4G/5G data — sold through prepaid and postpaid plans under its dual Robi and Airtel brands, alongside a growing digital-services portfolio: a "Single App" platform, Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) home broadband recently expanded through an integration with Starlink, and enterprise connectivity/ICT solutions for corporate clients.
ROBI.buyers: A mass-market base of 57.4 million mobile subscribers (39.9 million of them on 4G) made up of individual retail customers, plus a separate enterprise segment of roughly 1.7 million business/corporate customers who buy connectivity and ICT services directly from Robi.
ROBI.future: Robi's stated priorities center on deepening its shift from telco to techco: it launched 5G service and expanded its AI-powered Single App platform in 2025, grew its Fixed Wireless Access footprint via the Starlink integration, and reports a zero-debt balance sheet (BDT 69,856 mn equity) that it points to as funding future growth. Its stated corporate vision is "Becoming the Preferred Digital Connectivity Provider in Bangladesh."
